title: Caring for elders
tomorrow: the doorbell rings mid-dinner. it's Uncle Hamza. now what?

segments.voice: Yesterday, honor guests: Abraham's calf came before the questions. Today, the eldest person in the kitchen, and the heaviest pot.
screen: `HONOR GUESTS.` → `NOW: THE ELDEST, THE HEAVIEST POT.`

segments.voice: The heavy pot, the stairs, and a grandmother who says: I'm not old. Help too much and it stings. Help too little and someone gets hurt. The Prophet ﷺ met an old man in a moment a lot like that, and what he did is quietly surprising. It's the day Mecca opened to him. Abu Bakr, his closest companion, brings his elderly father, Abu Quhafa, to meet him, leading him by the hand.
screen: `I'M NOT OLD.` → `TOO MUCH, OR TOO LITTLE?` → `ABU QUHAFA, LED BY THE HAND.`

segments.voice: The Prophet looks at the old man and says to Abu Bakr: why didn't you leave him in his house, so I could go to him? Hear that again. The man everyone in the city wants to see offers to do the walking, so the elder doesn't have to. Abu Bakr answers that it's more fitting for his father to come. So the Prophet seats the old man in front of him. That's caring for elders in one scene: honor first, then help. A hadith in Tirmidhi says it in a line: whoever doesn't show mercy to our young and know the right of our elders isn't one of us. Know their right. Not take over their life. Another report, in Sunan Abu Dawud, counts honoring a gray-haired Muslim as part of glorifying God. So, back to the pot. Snatching it out of her hands can say: you're useless now. Watching her struggle on the stairs isn't honor either. The Prophet's move sits between: offer to come to her. Carry it together, let her lead, and take the heavy side. One to tell a friend tonight: on the day Mecca opened to him, the Prophet offered to walk to an old man's house.
screen: `I COULD HAVE COME TO HIM.` · `SEATED BEFORE HIM.` · `KNOW THE RIGHT OF ELDERS.` · `HONOR FIRST, THEN HELP.` · then, large: `CARE FOR ELDERS.`

segments.voice: Listen for one sound in the room, a hum, a voice far off, your own breath, and stay with it. Then bring to mind an elder you know and the sound of their voice: how they say your name, a phrase they always use. Hold it for the rest of the time, like something you don't want to lose.
screen: `ONE SOUND IN THE ROOM.` · `AN ELDER'S VOICE.` · `HOW THEY SAY YOUR NAME.`

segments.voice: Caring for elders: honoring older people first, then helping, the way the Prophet offered to go to Abu Quhafa.
Your line: care for elders, honor first and then the heavy pot, together. See you for the last of ten.

screen: `DAY 1720 COUNTS.` → `FAMILY AND FRIENDSHIP · 9 OF 10.` → `TOMORROW: THE DOORBELL RINGS. IT'S UNCLE HAMZA.`

howItsDone: Muslim families honor elders by greeting them first, serving them first and giving them the best seat at the table.

fork.setup: your grandfather insists on driving himself to the masjid, but his eyesight has been slipping. what fits 'know the right of elders'?
options: say nothing; questioning an elder is disrespectful.
hide his keys without telling him; safety beats feelings.
offer to drive him yourself, and ask to keep going with him.
fork.reveal: the Prophet offered to come to the old man. honor and help together: you go to him, and he still goes where he wanted.

chat.says: Dadi's hauling the big biryani pot upstairs for tomorrow. says 'i'm not old.' do i just let her?
options: Offer your arm and carry it with her. Honor first, then help.
Take it from her. Caring for elders means doing it all for them.
Let her. Respecting elders means never second-guessing them.
chat.meaning: The Prophet offered to walk to Abu Quhafa so the old man wouldn't have to. Elders are honored first, then helped.

Mecca.meaning: the Prophet's birthplace, home of the Ka'bah

Tirmidhi.meaning: Jami' at-Tirmidhi, a major collection of hadith

sources.ref: Musnad Ahmad (Asma' bint Abi Bakr: on the day of the opening of Mecca, Abu Bakr brought his father; 'why did you not leave the old man in his house so I could go to him?')
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1919–1920 (not one of us who shows no mercy to our young and does not know the right of our elders)
Sunan Abu Dawud 4843 (honoring a gray-haired Muslim is part of glorifying God)
